title: stable-diffusion.cpp .ckpt loader -- T1005 missing bounds check reads past the metadata buffer
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-47748 (GHSA-rx4w-x86j-vx57,
CVSS 5.5 MEDIUM), affecting stable-diffusion.cpp prior to
master-584-0a7ae07.

Unlike the sign-confusion write bugs in this corpus's other
`stable_diffusion_cpp_ckpt_*` rules, this is an OUT-OF-BOUNDS READ with
a different root cause: throughout the pickle `.ckpt` parser in
`src/model.cpp`, opcode handlers advance the parser position with
expressions like `buffer += N` WITHOUT first checking that
`buffer + N <= buffer_end`. A truncated `.ckpt` file -- simply cut
short, no sign-confusion trickery needed -- causes reads past the end
of the metadata buffer. The advisory notes LibFuzzer found crashes in
under one second of fuzzing against malformed checkpoint inputs, which
is itself a signal of how shallow this bug class is to trigger.

Detection logic flags the same coarse file-event signal as this
corpus's sibling `.ckpt`-loading rules -- a `.ckpt` file loaded by a
stable-diffusion.cpp process -- since host-level logging cannot
distinguish this specific opcode-advancement bug from the sign-
confusion bugs in the same file; all three are named as separate CVEs
because each is a distinct code defect, even though the detectable
artifact (a `.ckpt` load) is identical.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (leejet, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact source file, the general opcode-
advancement pattern, and the LibFuzzer finding), fixed in
master-584-0a7ae07 (same commit as the sibling rules).
